description: Quote-safe language presets for AI Mortgage Review Caller. Ensures compliant, approved language for rate discussions.

range_only.description: Use when borrower is eligible and we can provide an indicative rate range
opener: Based on what we know so far, I can share an estimated range — not a commitment — and Tim will confirm the exact terms on the review.
I can give you a rough range that's common for similar scenarios, and then Tim will validate what you actually qualify for.
Looking at the general picture, I can give you a ballpark range — the exact rate depends on details Tim will confirm during your review.
range_phrase: Something like {rate_range_text} depending on details like credit, equity, and the property.
Typically we're seeing something in the {rate_range_text} range for situations like yours, but that depends on the specifics.
For scenarios like yours, rates generally fall in the {rate_range_text} area — Tim will nail down exactly where you land.
close: If you want, we can lock in a quick {duration}-minute review to confirm it precisely.
The fastest way to get your exact number is a quick {duration}-minute review with Tim.
Want to set up a {duration}-minute call with Tim to lock in your actual rate?

ballpark.description: Use when we don't have enough detail to quote even a range
opener: I don't have enough detail to quote even a range yet, but I can explain the direction and what we'd need to confirm.
Without a few more details, I can't responsibly give you numbers — but I can tell you what factors into it.
I want to be straight with you — I'd need a bit more info before I could even ballpark this, but here's how it works.
close: The fastest way is a quick {duration}-minute review — Tim can confirm numbers with your exact profile.
A short {duration}-minute review with Tim is the best way to get you real numbers.
If you've got {duration} minutes, Tim can run through your specifics and give you something concrete.

no_quote.description: Use when we cannot or should not quote any numbers
opener: I can't responsibly quote numbers off this call without a couple key details and Tim's review — I don't want to mislead you.
I'd rather not throw out numbers without the full picture — that wouldn't be fair to you.
Without reviewing your specific situation, any number I give you would just be a guess, and I don't want to do that.
close: If it's worth it, we'll find out fast in a quick {duration}-minute review.
The only way to know for sure is a quick {duration}-minute review — no pressure, just clarity.
A {duration}-minute review with Tim will tell you exactly where you stand.

annual_mortgage_review.description: Annual check-up for existing mortgage holders
value_prop: This is more of a check-up than a sales call — we'll confirm whether anything improves your plan, and if not, we'll say so quickly.
Think of this as a quick health check on your mortgage — we'll see if anything's changed that could benefit you, and if not, no harm done.
We do these reviews to make sure you're still in the best position — sometimes things change, sometimes they don't.

rate_term_refi_review.description: Standard rate and term refinance opportunity
value_prop: Rates and pricing move; this is a quick review to see if there's a realistic benefit or if staying put is best.
The goal here is simple — see if current rates would actually save you money, or if your current loan is still the smart play.
We're looking at whether the math works for a refi — sometimes it does, sometimes it doesn't, and we'll tell you straight.
This is a strategy review — not just rate — to map payment, cash needs, and options without guessing.
Cash-out is more than just rate — it's about what you need the money for and how that affects your overall plan.
We'll look at how much you could access, what it would cost, and whether it actually makes sense for your situation.
Getting pre-approved gives you a real number to shop with — sellers take you seriously and you know your budget.
This is about knowing exactly what you qualify for before you fall in love with a house you can't get.
Pre-approval puts you in the driver's seat — you'll know your rate, your payment, and your buying power.
This is a safety review before the adjustment window — the goal is to avoid surprises.
Your rate is going to adjust soon, and we want to make sure you know your options before that happens.
Let's look at what your payment could become and whether there's a smarter move before the adjustment hits.

equity_strategy_review.description: High equity homeowners for strategic planning
value_prop: Equity changes over time; this is a quick strategy map of options and tradeoffs.
You've built up significant equity — let's look at what you could do with it and whether any of it makes sense for you.
This is about understanding your options — consolidation, improvements, investments — and the real costs of each.
Think of this as a tune-up — we'll check if anything's changed that could save you money or reduce risk.
Markets move, your situation changes — this is a quick check to see if your mortgage is still optimized.
We're just making sure you're not leaving money on the table with your current setup.

rate_watch.description: Borrowers actively watching rates for opportunity
value_prop: You've been watching rates — let's see if we've hit the number that makes sense for your situation.
The market's been moving — this is a good time to check if the math finally works for you.
We've hit some interesting rate levels — worth a quick look to see if now's the time.

disclaimer_templates.default: This is an estimate, not a commitment to lend. Final terms depend on your application, documentation, and underwriting.
disclaimer_templates.short: Estimate only — final terms depend on full review.
disclaimer_templates.detailed: This is an estimate for discussion purposes only, not a commitment to lend. Actual rates, payments, and terms are subject to credit approval, property appraisal, and verification of income and assets. Terms may change based on market conditions.

state_specific.TX: This is an estimate only. Texas home equity loans are subject to specific requirements including the 80% combined loan-to-value limit.
state_specific.CA: This is an estimate only. California requires specific disclosures which will be provided as part of the formal application process.

to_booking: Want to take the next step?
Should we get you on Tim's calendar?
Ready to see what your numbers actually look like?

too_busy: I get it — that's exactly why we keep it to {duration} minutes. If it's not worth your time, we'll know fast.
Totally understand. The review is quick — {duration} minutes — and you'll have clarity either way.
not_interested: Fair enough. Mind if I ask what changed since you reached out?
No problem at all. Just curious — is it timing, or did you find something better?
need_to_think: Absolutely. What would help you decide?
Of course. Is there specific information that would help you think it through?

compliance_notes.rate_context: Always present rates as ranges or estimates. Never quote a single rate as if it's guaranteed. Use phrases like 'typically', 'generally', 'in the range of'.
